answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using verifiable proof-of-space. Participating nodes commit unique pseudo-random sectors inside a local storage vault, regularly answering challenge queries to stay above a consensus ledge. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of procuring physical drive capacity and sustained read-write bandwidth per identity as deployment scales toward its zenith. However, this design incentivizes centralized hardware pooling and penalizes lightweight agents.
